The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Kalshi CEO says state-led oversight of U.S. prediction markets would push them out. CEO Tarek Mansour said he feels "pretty good" about the pending outcome of the current legal fight over who has the right to regulate prediction markets. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

AI agents make 138 million crypto payments as U.S. dominates spending on AI models. U.S.-linked wallets account for just over 88% of tracked AI model payments, dwarfing China’s 0.1% share, according to new Chainalysis research. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto Long & Short: Why gold and bitcoin belong in the same portfolio. The report adds another detail to the day's market picture. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

EasyA hits $1.1 billion valuation, targets 2027 public listing and tokenized shares. The blockchain and AI developer platform has completed two years of audits and wants its shares available onchain from the first day of trading. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

BlackRock's crypto ETF assets surge 63% but remain far below 2025 peak. The asset manager's crypto assets surged 63% to $79.6 billion as investors returned, but holdings remain 23% below year-ago levels. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Former FTX Europe chief targets U.S. tokenized stock trading with new SEC exemption. Nasdaq-listed Perpetuals.com is the second company to pursue a U.S. tokenized stock marketplace under the SEC's new framework, following a joint venture between OKX and NYSE parent ICE. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $81,536 with a -1.93% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,428.65 with a -3.13% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.description:
Title: Crypto News Today: Japan Pushes Yen Stablecoins and Crypto ETFs in Bold Market Shift
# Crypto News Today: Japan Pushes Yen Stablecoins and Crypto ETFs in Bold Market Shift. ## Japan's ruling party wants yen stablecoins used for Asia settlements and seeks a legal path for crypto ETFs. The proposal aims to expand blockchain use. SoftBank-linked payment rails could help connect users to the new market. Japan’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) has urged the government to promote yen-based stablecoins for settlements across Asia and create a legal framework for cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs). The proposal, submitted to Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama on Monday, seeks to expand Japan’s role in digital finance while supporting blockchain innovation. The recommendations also position crypto ETFs as an official investment product within the country’s financial markets. The LDP’s blockchain technology promotion panel presented the proposal to Katayama, who also oversees Japan’s Financial Services Agency (FSA). The panel stated that crypto ETFs could offer investors a simple and familiar way to gain exposure to digital assets without directly holding cryptocurrencies. Meanwhile, lawmaker Junichi Kanda said Japan should use the Asian Development Bank’s annual meeting next May to showcase progress in blockchain technology and yen-based stablecoins. He told reporters that the government should take steps to encourage the future use of yen stablecoins for settlements across Asia. A crypto ETF allows investors to access cryptocurrency markets through a regulated financial product. The proposal arrives as the FSA continues to support blockchain-based innovation among domestic financial institutions. The initiative aims to explore practical uses for digital currencies within the financial system. However, policymakers have warned that stablecoins could move funds outside regulated banking channels and reduce the role of commercial banks in international payment networks. In October 2025, PayPay, SoftBank’s payments subsidiary, acquired a 40% stake in Binance Japan. PayPay serves more than 70 million users, giving the company a large presence in Japan’s digital payments market. As policymakers discuss new rules, existing payment networks and distribution channels could play a central role in bringing digital financial products to consumers. Japan’s ruling party is pushing yen stablecoins for regional settlements and a legal framework for crypto ETFs, signaling a broader shift toward blockchain-led finance.

items.title: Ripple (XRP) on the Edge: Can It Survive Regulation, ETFs and Stablecoins?
items.description:
Title: Ripple (XRP) on the Edge: Can It Survive Regulation, ETFs and Stablecoins?
# Ripple (XRP) on the Edge: Can It Survive Regulation, ETFs and Stablecoins? Ripple’s XRP is back in the spotlight with legal battles, stablecoin ambitions and ETF rumors reshaping its future. Ripple’s XRP has re-entered the global crypto conversation as regulatory pressure, institutional interest and new product launches collide. From the long-running SEC lawsuit to fresh talk around stablecoins and ETFs, XRP stands at a critical crossroads that could redefine its role in the digital asset ecosystem. XRP is trading in an environment defined by regulatory uncertainty, shifting liquidity, and aggressive competition from other layer-1 and payments-focused networks. In this volatile backdrop, trader sentiment tends to flip quickly, with XRP frequently reacting to headlines about the SEC case, macro liquidity conditions, and broader crypto risk appetite rather than purely technical signals. YouTube: Search "XRP Ripple price analysis". TikTok: Search "XRP Ripple crypto". Globally, however, XRP remains actively traded. A key strategic question is whether a Ripple stablecoin could cannibalize XRP demand. Following the rise of spot Bitcoin and, in some regions, Ethereum-focused exchange-traded products, the market has increasingly speculated about whether an XRP-based ETF or similar regulated vehicle could eventually emerge. However, the unresolved or evolving aspects of the SEC case and the broader regulatory classification of XRP remain key obstacles, especially in the U.S. Until those issues are clearly settled, many analysts expect continued delays or cautious stances from regulators on ETF-like structures. Under this scenario, XRP could reclaim a stronger role as a cross-border liquidity asset and regain market share among the top digital assets by capitalization. In this environment, XRP could underperform the broader market, with capital rotating into assets seen as having clearer regulatory standing or stronger on-chain growth. For investors and traders, the rational stance is to treat XRP as a high-beta, high-uncertainty asset linked to ongoing regulatory developments, macro liquidity, and Ripple’s execution on products such as stablecoins and institutional payment rails. As 2026 progresses, the combination of regulatory clarity, progress on stablecoins like RLUSD, and potential moves toward more regulated investment vehicles will determine whether XRP can evolve from a lawsuit headline token back into a core component of global digital payments infrastructure.

# Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Price Predictions Today: Why Is Crypto Falling?

Coin Gabbar

Coin Gabbar@coin\_gabbar\_·

The crypto market took a step back today. The total market cap fell to $2.76 trillion, down 0.60% in the past 24 hours. Trading volume sits at $94.41 billion.

Bitcoin slipped to $78,062.80. Ethereum eased to $2,470.13. XRP dropped to $1.38. Most coins are red today, but the drop is mild, not a crash.

### Why is Crypto Market Down Today? [...] Ethereum trades at $2,472.04 today, down 1.80%. The coin has been stuck between $2,400 and $2,550 for over a week now.

Retail selling and a slowdown in demand from bigger buyers seem to be the main reasons for the sideways action.

Near-term resistance sits around $2,520 to $2,530. That level has rejected price several times in recent weeks. Each retest without a sharp rejection tends to weaken resistance over time, which raises the odds of an eventual breakout. [...] Markets are now pricing in a 60.4% chance of a rate hike at the September 16 Fed meeting, up from 39.6% odds of no change.

A month ago, the odds were close to a coin flip. Now, the market thinks a hike is more likely than not. Higher rates usually mean less money flowing into risk assets like crypto.

### Is the crypto market in fear or greed right now?

The Fear & Greed Index shows a score of 69 today. That puts the market in Greed territory.
